HRA Analysis: OVERVIEW:ROCKIN GEMMA (10) has her first start for the new stable and looks very well placed against her own sex, particularly with the concession claim. She punches through behind a very quick beginner, so she should map within striking distance. She showed some ability last preparation after coming to Victoria and, in her one trial for the Matt Horsnell camp, trialled very well against a couple of smart ones at Terang recently in a good tune-up for this. GOLD IN PARIS (6) partnered with James Herbertson for the first time and duly saluted last time out with gusto, beating home HUXHAM CHUBB (7), who was also very good as runner-up. That horse has since franked the form by winning at Charlton last Monday, and that pair appear the testing material, albeit from awkward draws. EASTBRO KAZ (11) is another benefiting from a concession in easier grade. She’s been racing against much better-quality opposition and can sweep home well with the right cover. QUICK CRUNCH (1) and MEGAWATTS (4) have hit a purple patch of form and are in the mix, while JILLIBY KYMY LOU (2) and TORQUE INTHEUSA (3) have the best speed and cut at each other last time, which could ensure a genuine tempo. BACK: ROCKIN GEMMA (10)– 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:ROCKIN GEMMA (10), GOLD IN PARIS (6), HUXHAM CHUBB (7), EASTBRO KAZ (11)

OVERVIEW: Very tricky affair, with the majority of these not winning out of turn. The experience of driver Michael Bellman is a major factor here from the positive draw, allowing him to press forward and look for the lead with MISSMALACHITE (3). She hasn’t had much luck with barrier draws and has been forced to work harder than she’d like, whereas the map and opposition here look favourable. Her last victory came back in April when she was able to find the top. ZWICK (4) can slide across with her and potentially map handy. He finds a better draw than he’s been used to and will also find this grade more to his liking. He’s also a winner at this track. YANKEE RAIN (7) stays under notice after switching to the Tom Rundle stable and has trialled okay leading into this, although the draw is a little tricky. BLISSFULL LILLY (5) was a winner when leading four starts back, so the map is important for her, while the draw for ICONMOTOR (2) helps him. They both have minor claims. SELECTIONS:MISSMALACHITE (3), ZWICK (4), YANKEE RAIN (7), ICONMOTOR (2)

OVERVIEW: Standing-start conditions for the trotters, where you can expect the likely leader after 600m to come from ALLAWART BOB (2), BROWN EYED KATE (3) and ITGETSBETTER (4), despite all being off 10 metres. However, those off the bigger handicaps have the better form. BOUTIKA (5) is one of those and will find this much more suitable than her last start at Melton. More compelling is the fact that the last time she started under standing-start conditions was at this track back in April, where she began well off the 20m handicap and beat her rivals easily. She looks well placed. JAKARTA (7) has regained some better form under standing-start conditions and won well off 30m back in July. Her starts since have been sound, so she must be considered. BARLINNE (6) ran second in that July win, and her past couple have looked tougher than this. Poor manners from the opposition bring the leaders ALLAWART BOB (2), BROWN EYED KATE (3) and ITGETSBETTER (4) into calculations, while backmarker SONAMI JOH (9) also ranks as a minor chance. BACK: BOUTIKA (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:BOUTIKA (5), JAKARTA (7), ITGETSBETTER (4), BARLINNE (6)

OVERVIEW: The inside four horses all like to show gate speed here, so the battle for the lead is very interesting, with three stablemates and DIRECT COMMAND (2) sandwiched in between them. With that in mind, I’m looking away from the leading division and expect sharp improvement from BACKBEACH PETER (7), who had nothing go right in his two recent runs in SA when failing as a short-priced favourite. I’m happy to overlook those and assess his prior performances, which were terrific. Most notable was a runner-up performance to Rocknroll Willow, who has since franked that form. GRINNING BEACH BOY (4) led from a better draw last time when second. He’s going to need things to work out, but Herbertson sticking with him is a major plus. DIRECT COMMAND (2) could be open to sharp improvement after coming up with his best draw in some time, and the last time he was able to find the top he was a winner back in June. FIVE CENT (5) gets another tricky draw but is racing honestly, as is PRECIOUS BELLE (6), who’s a get-back type. Both have minor claims. BACK: BACKBEACH PETER (7)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:BACKBEACH PETER (7), GRINNING BEACH BOY (4), DIRECT COMMAND (2), PRECIOUS BELLE (6)

OVERVIEW: Tricky affair with 2yos taking on 3yos and a few without exposed form. BAY LA VILLE (8) is a 3yo filly first-up without a trial, but what she displayed last preparation deserves respect. She won on debut, where she settled back in the field and found the line strongly, beating a reasonable field. At her next assignment in the Vicbred Super Series she underperformed and was thrown in the paddock. Whilst the fitness may not be there, the ability is. COCO MILLER (1) is a 2yo filly who has trialled very well leading into a race of this calibre. She’s stepped out three times and has won each of those trials, displaying good manners, while in her past two trials she was able to record a reasonable mile rate. The barrier draw means she maps well, and being on the peg line over the sprint trip is an advantage. RAVISHING ROXY (6) will appreciate getting back to age-assessed racing after two runs up in class this preparation, the most recent of which saw her run third. She’s mixed her gate speed, leading on occasions and beginning roughly in others, but she’s in the mix. SWEET LADY LOU (7) was able to win at her sixth start as a 2yo and found the line well from back and wide. She’s had the benefit of one run this preparation and hit the line okay in what was a stronger field than she meets here. The draw is a little tricky, however. SELECTIONS: BAY LA VILLE (8), COCO MILLER (1), RAVISHING ROXY (6), SWEET LADY LOU (7)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY ECLIPSE (8) started a very short-priced favourite on debut and did everything wrong, galloping twice in the run when she was about to obtain a good position. She’s had two trials since then and showed marked improvement in her manners. She will no doubt be short odds again, courtesy of the power of the Lee stable alone, but tread warily given her manners. SHEER ME (5) comes here with different form, having her first start for the new stable after arriving from NSW. She’s a well-bred mare coming in without a trial, but keep her safe and watch the betting. SPORTY ROCKS (3) has run some decent races, placing twice, and should get a decent map in a race that doesn’t appear overly strong. JADES REASON (2) is a 2yo filly taking on the older horses, and she wasn’t too bad last time out at Globe Derby, sitting parked for the final lap against a reasonable field and battling to the line okay. The soft draw helps. SELECTIONS: JILLIBY ECLIPSE (8), SHEER ME (5), SPORTY ROCKS (3), JADES REASON (2)

OVERVIEW:IMALLATTITUDE (5) has been racing in terrific form lately and finds another suitable race to be a strong winning hope. Sectionally, he was terrific last start, narrowly missed with a flat tyre the start prior and was a winner three back when Luke Sutherland was aboard, who claims again here. Whilst he will be at the mercy of the right tempo in a small field, the way he’s been running on suggests he will be hard to hold out. PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (1) is a lightning-quick beginner and won’t be crossed from the pole. It depends on what tactics Jackie Barker wants to adopt from there, but either way he presents as the hardest to run down. IAMAWINGATE (2) was disappointing at Shepparton, but he always seems to come back into his best form when racing at this grade, and reuniting with Herbertson adds appeal, as he was the last driver to win on him. JUST LIKE NUGGET (4) finally broke through for his maiden win when given a perfect run; however, this map looks a little sticky if he’s to get a similar trip. BACK: IMALLATTITUDE (5)– 3.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: IMALLATTITUDE (5), PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (1), IAMAWINGATE (2), JUST LIKE NUGGET (4)

OVERVIEW: Problematic way to finish, with most of these clashing in a race at Ballarat two runs back, so there’s a form line there, but subsequently they’ve all performed poorly at their next outing. Hence why I want to look away from that race, and it leaves me with DOCTOR GO JOH (7), who comes into the race with the best national rating and will find this company much more suitable. He’s had to sit parked in fast times his past couple, times which this opposition is unlikely to be able to match. In his last win in June, he defeated a horse who won easily earlier in the week. SIR CANDY CLOUD (5) did burn early trying to find the lead last time out, so there are reasons to forgive that performance. Bellman jumps aboard for the first time and could assist in a change of form. ALLTHEWAYTOROYALTY (2) was good at his first run for the stable but then performed poorly at Mildura when he led and over raced as favourite. He could improve if he brings his best. DI ANGELO (4) hasn’t had the best passage in running his past couple and is familiar with this company, so he’s in the mix. SELECTIONS:DOCTOR GO JOH (7), SIR CANDY CLOUD (5), ALLTHEWAYTOROYALTY (2), DI ANGELO (4)

OMNIA (4) was extremely impressive first up from a spell last start at Gawler. She defeated JILLIBY BLISS by 3.1 meter after facing the breeze. She will be hard to beat again today if she can back her last start up. JILLIBY BLISS (3) is improving with each run she has here in South Australia. She could be a major improver today. EAGLESTONE (2) and PLATINUMS SON (5) are also chances.

MAJESTIC SUMMER (6) finds a much easier race tonight compared to her recent assignments. The handicap will be a little tricky but she is good enough to win a race like this. HURRICANE JANE (2) looks like the main danger after an impressive last start win. THE CLIPPER (3) and DOUBLE JOEY (4) are also chances.

SHIRLEY NOT (6) doesn’t have the best draw tonight but her she ran a handy race last start behind OUR CHEEKY DEVIL. She looks ready to bounce back into the winners list today. MEET ME AT THE BEACH (2) is well drawn and she looks like the main danger. SWEET ARPEGGIO (4) and LUNCHINHEAVEN (1) are also chances.

BLINGADINGDING (5) did it tough from the second row last start at Gawler when he finished 5.6 meters behind COME ON BILLEE. He should be able to improve off that run though and be around the mark today. LUNADIVA (2) gets her best chance to win a race today. She is well drawn and she has been showing signs that she is getting closer to a win. CLARENDEN ARCADIA (3) and SPIRIT OF SASSY (1) are also chances.

STAR MAN (1) was run down by HARRO HILL and a few others last start after leading. He should be able to lead again today. Today is a more winnable race for him over a more suitable distance. MAGIC STORM (5), CENTREFOLD STAR (2) and AMIRA MARIE (3) are also chances.

OAKLANDER (6) has got the draw to hopefully find a handy position in the running line early and just sit back and watch the early speed unfold. The possible leaders can all easily be run down so he should be charging home late. He should be hard to beat. NEED ME SOME SUGAR (4) could easily pop up and win a race like this if she is at her best. SEA HUNTER (8) and LORD MYRMECIA (3) are also chances.

LOCHINVAR RULER (2) has been running around the mark recently. He gets Ryan Hryhorec back in the sulky and he is well drawn. He is worth strong consideration in such an even race. TRIGGER (7), STAR OF WILLOUGHBY (5) and LUCKY BAMBINO (4) are also chances.

LIGHTNING BLING (4) wasn’t in his best form last start at Port Pirie but his two runs before that were superb. If he can lob into the right position today then he is a big chance. JUST BECCY (1) is first up but she has trialled well and she should be dangerous from the inside draw. GRUMPYPANTS GRACIE (6) and HELLO BEAUTIFUL (5) are also chances. The maiden two-year-olds kick-start the night, where CREAMY KARALTA (7) makes his debut following two impressive trial. He draws the outside of the front row, but looks a classy type and expect Kent Rattray to have him screwed down and ready to win first up. RYHAD (1) trialled nicely against older horses in good time recently and should take plenty of improvement from that experience, although he showed limited gate speed on that occasion. SOLO SNITCH (2) and IDEN JUST BECAUSE (8) drop back in grade after competing in recent two-year-old features and should appreciate their favourable draws, giving both every opportunity to be in the finish. POGACAR (6) and SMELL THE SMOKE (4) have both placed at the trials and look like improving types. It would be no surprise to see either take another step forward here, and they appear the best of the remainder. Selections:CREAMY KARALTA (7), SOLO SNITCH (2), IDEN JUST BECAUSE (8), RYHAD (1) Staking Strategy:CREAMY KARALTA looks promising off his two trials and, even from the wide gate, should take plenty of holding out late. 3 unit win – CREAMY KARALTA (7)

GO THE RED (2) has been a great addition to the Yole stable since arriving from Queensland and produced another handy performance in similar grade against some classy opposition last start. Expect him to be driven aggressively again here in an attempt to find the front, where he could take plenty of running down over the longer distance. ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (5) is a brilliant standing-start beginner and should find himself in the first couple after 200 metres. He should relish the longer journey and looks certain to be thereabouts. GORDONS BAY (6) comes from the 20-metre back mark but should get every opportunity in the small field to utilise his sharp finishing sprint. IRON CLAD (1) is rarely far away in races of this nature, as is COLBY SANZ (3), while WATERMELON SUGAR (4) could give a cheeky sight if he begins sharply, as he has done on a couple of occasions recently. Selections:GO THE RED (2), ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (5), GORDONS BAY (6), IRON CLAD (1) Staking Strategy:GO THE RED continues to impress and should take plenty of beating from the front handicap here. 2 unit win – GO THE RED (2)

The maidens again go at it looking to break their duck, with several runners knocking on the door. CHARLI PIPPEN (5) continues to threaten to break through but has kept finding one better. Expect him to settle just off the speed with cover and get another opportunity to finish strongly. LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (3) will no doubt look to attempt an all-the-way victory, as he has done on several occasions recently, while LITTLE CAPPUCCINA (2) should also settle handy on the pegs and has not been far away of late. QUARTEIRA (7) is a well-bred three-year-old colt closely related to the champion Beautide and should continue to improve with further race experience. Recent mainland arrivals DIAMONDONTHEROCKS (8) and ROBUST SALLY (9) should be competitive in a maiden of this nature. DEMON DESTROYER (6) has changed stables and, although he has clearly had some gait issues throughout his short career, he was seen making nice ground in a trial earlier this week. If he brings his best manners and form to race night, he could be right in the finish. Selections:CHARLI PIPPEN (5), LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (3), DEMON DESTROYER (6), LITTLE CAPPUCCINA (2) Staking Strategy: There has been good early support for DEMON DESTROYER following a nice trial, so happy to play that way. 2 unit win – DEMON DESTROYER (6)

An even field where the three-year-olds A DRAGON FOR JOE (3) and OMYBACNKNEES JUDGE (2) will be looking to take advantage of their favourable front-row draws after some handy performances of late. Expect KEAYANG LEXI (1) to attempt to control the race from the front, while IFYOULOVEMELETMEGO (4) should also be driven forward from the gate. That should give the three-year-olds their opportunity to secure positions on speed with cover and be right in the finish. JET TO HEAVEN (10) makes his Tasmanian debut for the visiting stable and brings handy enough mainland form to be competitive in a race of this nature. It wouldn't surprise to see any of the remaining runners bob up and earn a cheque for connections in what looks a very even affair. Selections A DRAGON FOR JOE (3), OMYBACNKNEES JUDGE (2), IFYOULOVEME LETMEGO (4), JET TO HEAVEN (10) Staking Strategy:A DRAGON FOR JOE should get a nice spot on speed with cover and gets his chance to get back in the winner's circle. 1 unit win – A DRAGON FOR JOE (3)

A competitive field with plenty of consistent performers engaged, where MUZZA MEMATE (4) is racing in career-best form. He can still be a nervous watch for punters and occasionally does something wrong, but clearly possesses the most ability in this field when at his best. Expect him to push forward from the draw, as will EVERYTHING BUT THE (2), who has been super consistent of late and may be able to find the pegs, where he could take plenty of running down and looks a danger. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (1) is always thereabouts in this grade and should again get his opportunity from a position on speed. MONEYS NO ISSUE (9) was spotted hitting the line strongly last start and should be running home well again, while MOVESLIKEALADY (12) will no doubt be doing similar from the wide back-row draw, as she usually does when saved for one run. JOHN VINCENT (10) is an interesting runner arriving from South Australia and looks to possess plenty of speed, so the market may be the best guide to his chances first up in the state. Selections:MUZZAMEMATE (4), EVERYTHING BUT THE (2), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (1)MONEYS NO ISSUE (9) Staking Strategy:EVERYTHING BUT THE has been super consistent and gets a nice draw, while MUZZAME MATE is in career-best form. Happy to have a dual play here. 2 unit win – MUZZAME MATE (4) & 1 unit win – EVERYTHING BUT THE (2)

The low-class event of the night is an extremely open affair. Expect PARK LANE (4) to use his sharp gate speed in an attempt to find the front, where he could give a cheeky sight at odds over the short distance and looks a potential improver. SHEEZA SOHO (1) should enjoy a nice run in transit behind the expected speed and gets her chance to notch up another victory, being the least-experienced runner in the field. JEREMY WELLS (5) and GOBSMACKED (7) should be running home strongly, as they usually do in races of this nature. COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2) gets his opportunity to improve from a favourable draw, while HORRIE OTARA (3) and CHRIS BE QUICK (6) should again run their usual honest races. Selections:SHEEZA SOHO (1), PARK LANE (4), COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2), GOBSMACKED (7) Staking Strategy: An absolute raffle here, but PARK LANE could run a cheeky race over the mile if he settles somewhat in running. 1 unit win – PARK LANE (4)

Trainer Charlie Castles holds the key here, with the stable appearing to have the two leading chances in the field. ATOMIC BLACK (1) possesses good gate speed and gets his chance to return to the winner's circle from the pole draw over the short trip. LOU BABY (4) should appreciate the smaller field and gets his opportunity to settle on speed and show his class after two handy performances since returning from a lengthy spell. He should now be nearing peak fitness. LYNRYD SKYNRYD (7) could be the fly in the ointment from a speed-map perspective if he is used aggressively from the gate, as he often is. ANOTHER NIEN (9) gets a nice trailing draw and is rarely far away in races of this nature. If there is genuine early speed, that should also suit SNOWIEWILLREV (2), who was an easy winner last start when coming off a hot tempo, albeit in weaker grade. He should receive another nice run in transit and be finishing off strongly. Likewise, VANQUISH STRIDE (3) can never be ruled out in this grade. Selections:ATOMIC BLACK (1), LOU BABY (4), SNOWIEWILLREV (2), VANQUISH STRIDE (3) Staking Strategy:LOU BABY can show his class here on speed after some good runs from bad draws so far this preparation. 2 unit win – LOU BABY (4)

WEE GEORGIE WOOD (1) will be looking to take advantage of getting back to a favourable draw and gets his chance to return to the winner's circle. He can be a little touchy behind the mobile, however, so will need to bring his best manners, particularly with ART HUNTSMAN (4) likely to use his sharp gate speed in an attempt to find the pegs early. He has returned to his best form of late and continues to race very consistently. WATCH YOUR BACK (5) got the gaps at the right time when winning last start and gets his opportunity to make it back-to-back victories in this even field. IMA LITTLE NEEDY (3) should find a position on speed with cover and gets his chance after competing well in recent four-year-old features, with this representing somewhat of a drop in class. The four Wayne Yole-trained runners can never be ruled out in races of this nature, with CAN FEEL THE FURY (6) looking the pick of them after returning to his best form in recent starts. He would appreciate genuine tempo throughout to allow him to finish off strongly. Selections:WEE GEORGIE WOOD (1), ART HUNTSMAN (4), IMA LITTLE NEEDY, WATCH YOUR BACK (5) Staking Strategy: If WEE GEORGIE WOOD brings his best behaviour, he could take plenty of running down. 1 unit win – WEE GEORGIE WOOD (1)

The No More Than Three Wins Fillies and Mares event brings together a fairly even field on ability, although there is a wider spread when it comes to their handicap marks. SOHO TIGER LILY (4) should be the first runner to the pegs after competing in the Oaks last start and gets her chance to run another strong race back in this company. ALWAYSATIGER (6) drops back from the four-year-old mares features and should be finishing strongly, noting she has also undergone a stable change since her latest appearance. WEONA EAGLE (7) could be the one at odds if she can rediscover her best form, while SWEETHEART DIOR (2) has been excellent in all her starts since arriving in Tasmania, including a handy third in the Oaks last week. ALL ABOUT SADIE (1) and PHLOW JO (5) are consistent mares who rarely run poorly and will again be looking to earn a cheque for connections by finishing in the placings. Selections:SWEETHEART DIOR (2), SOHO TIGERLILY (4), ALWAYSATIGER (6), PHLOW JO (5) Staking Strategy:SWEETHEART DIOR ran nicely in the Oaks and gets her chance from a good draw here. 2 unit win – SWEETHEART DIOR (2) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:KYVALLEY DIXON (7) is a quality filly, which has had two wins from her past three starts and looms as a strong winning chance again. She won convincingly over Remembrance Time at Melton on July 11 and won a trial at Kilmore on Tuesday. ALDEBARAN EMJAY (6) was a runaway winner on debut then competed in the Nutrien Classic, where she finished in fourth after trailing the leader, being in a clear third but broke stride on the home turn. She hasn’t raced since May but would have benefited from two recent trial efforts and will take beating if she is somewhere near her peak. TRUE APLOMB (4) is resuming since a third at Maryborough in May but she was impressive at a Kilmore trial victory, where she settled down last and sustained a strong run from the 600m mark. She is a speedy type and is worth a ticket each way. CLOUDY CANYON (5) led out then took cover and won on debut then followed with a distant fourth behind KYVALLEY DIXON (7). He has early speed and is not without a chance. BACK: KYVALLEY DIXON (7) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY DIXON (7), ALDEBARAN EMJAY (6), TRUE APLOMB (4), CLOUDY CANYON (5)

OVERVIEW:THE NIGHT FOX (5) is a former New Zealand pacer, which boasts sound North Island form and should run a good race on his Australian debut. He went forward at the start then was shuffled back on the markers mid-race at his latest Cambridge performance. WICKED MITZI (2) finished off well for second behind Shazza Love at Kilmore last outing. She possesses early speed and is drawn to receive every chance so she is capable of going one better. OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (3) was shuffled to three back on the markers and finished off reasonably well for fifth behind Pistol Pearce last outing. He attempted to lead throughout when second behind the smart filly Rocknroll Willow (won again since) at Stawell three starts ago. He is a good chance of working to the lead again and is worth an investment. IN AN IDEAL WORLD (8) performs best when he is able to lead so being drawn on the second line is a disadvantage but he has the ability to figure in the finish. SELECTIONS: THE NIGHT FOX (5), WICKED MITZI (2), OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (3), IN AN IDEAL WORLD (8)

OVERVIEW: PURPLE MOON (2) will appreciate a big drop back in class on her latest fourth in a $50,000 event at Menangle on July 04. She was a winner at Menangle two starts ago and is drawn to go close again. ZOOLU (6) is resuming since a fifth at Bendigo in June. She competed in the New South Wales Oaks back in May and led throughout at a Maryborough victory in April so she must be respected. MISTER DEVEREAUX (8) is awkwardly drawn but is racing well enough to figure in the finish. He progressed forward from a wide draw to find the lead when he scored at Kilmore three starts ago and he was placed behind the smart trotter The Preacher at his latest performance. VAPAR JOHN (9) showed ability at his debut, where he made up late ground for third. He should have improved by the experience and is worth an investment from his trailing draw. BACK: PURPLE MOON (2) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: PURPLE MOON (2), ZOOLU (6), MISTER DEVEREAUX (8), VAPAR JOHN (9)

OVERVIEW: DAISY STARZZZ (10) worked hard at various stages of the event and battled on fairly well for fourth at Cranbourne last week. She should be fitter after having two starts since October 2023 and looms as one of the leading chances. BETTING ATTACK (6) began quickly and attempted to lead throughout when third behind Just Like Nugget at Charlton last week. He is a good chance of finding the lead again and this race is no harder. MAHEO (4) trailed the leader and finished in third behind Wottawizard at her debut then broke stride from behind the leader and lost her chance at Charlton. She went well enough first up to suggest she should be competitive against this line up. KAIDENBOY (2) is a first starter for trainer Jason Ainsworth, which has performed fairly well at the trials with the latest being a second at Hamilton, and is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: DAISY STARZZZ (10), BETTING ATTACK (6), MAHEO (4), KAIDENBOY (2)

OVERVIEW:SMOKING SHANNON (1) made a big impression at her Victorian debut as she led throughout and blitzed her rivals in a mile rate of 1.55.7 at Shepparton. She is drawn to lead again and will take catching. ASMILEANDAWINX (7) is dropping back in class from her recent efforts at Metropolitan level and is capable of improving on her numerical form. Her third placed effort behind Keayang Payton in a mile rate of 1.54.1 is a good form pointer for this event. OLIVIA ROSE (5) is an interesting runner. She hasn’t started since sprinting sharply down the back straight and sustaining the run to score impressively at Terang in December. She has a tricky draw first up but is too good to dismiss. OPTIMAL (3) finished off quickly from midfield on the markers when third behind the smart pacer Secret Service Agent at Geelong and is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: SMOKING SHANNON (1), ASMILEANDAWINX (7), OLIVIA ROSE (5), OPTIMAL (3)

OVERVIEW:KYVALLEY MISTY (11) is resuming since a disappointing last of nine at Bendigo in June. She was placed behind Mista Walker from the standing start at Cranbourne on May 24 and she finished second at a recent Kilmore trial performance so she is worth thought against this line up. SUZYS DREAM (7) was heavily supported ($1-45 fav) and faded after racing without cover at Kilmore last outing. She is dropping back into a suitable class and gets her chance to improve on her numerical form. BETSY ANNE (8) will appreciate a drop back in class from her past three attempts and she was runner up behind the in-form trotter Champagnes on July 23 so she is worth an investment. CHARLIE WALKER (10) is resuming since a third at Ballarat in May. He is usually competitive against this class and will go close if he is somewhere near his peak. SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY MISTY (11), SUZYS DREAM (7), BETSY ANNE (8), CHARLIE WALKER (10)

OVERVIEW: THE FIERY SUNSET (2) hasn’t had a great deal of luck at her past few outings and performs best when she is close to the pace so she gets her chance to improve from the good draw. She defeated Pique and Silent Reverie (won since) at a Geelong victory on July 03. MAJOR MAX (10) was having his first run in a month when he was able to run home best and defeat Love Who (won since) at Kilmore. His manners frequently let him down but he is a strong chance if he delivers another fool proof display. NIGHT SKY (3) has performed below her best form in two starts back from a break but she has been competitive against stronger grade previously and she should be getting fitter. WHATSTHEGOSS (9) was in a striking position but broke stride at the 300m when unplaced at Maryborough last outing. He is racing better than his form reads and is worth thought. LOUIEVILLE LASS (4) and BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (6) are both capable of showing up without surprising. If the emergency MASSIF CENTRAL (5) gains a start, he should be in front for a long way. SELECTIONS: THE FIERY SUNSET (2), MAJOR MAX (10), NIGHT SKY (3), WHATSTHEGOSS (9)

OVERVIEW: MUSKEE (11) is new to the standing start but he will take beating if he begins safely. He finished fast to score at Melton two starts ago then followed with a third behind the very smart trotter Alrighty. ANTONOV (6) boasts very consistent form from behind the tapes and is versatile. He made a mid-race move and parked without cover when a game second behind John’s Boy last outing. JUST AS I AM (8) lacks standing start experience but has been racing against strong opposition and should be competitive if he can trot away in the desired manner. JACK SPRAT (9) is a strong type and worked forward to find the lead when he scored at Melton two starts ago. He will be suited if there is a genuine tempo throughout. WATCH AND ACT (1) and MAESTRO (10) are both standing start specialists and cannot be left out of calculations. BACK: MUSKEE (11) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: MUSKEE (11), ANTONOV (6), JUST AS I AM (8), JACK SPRAT (9)

OVERVIEW: DONA AMALIA (10) struck trouble and lost his chance when seventh at Kilmore last outing. He finished off strongly when a game second behind Jilliby Topgun prior so he appears to be hard to beat against this line up. POPPY POPSTAR (9) tired after racing without cover at Kilmore last outing but she was a big winner at Maryborough when working hard in the run prior and she has won five races under similar conditions this season. RASTAMON (4) is a fast beginner and will take catching if he is able to find the lead. He attempted to lead early, ended up being behind the leader from the 1300m and finished in fourth at Ballarat last week. VAN DOREN (2) is trotting consistently and is drawn to gain a trail just off the speed. He is worth thought along with MORNING DOVE (5), QUEEN TRUSCOTT (7) and BLACK AND GOLD (11). BACK: DONA AMALIA (10) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: DONA AMALIA (10), POPPY POPSTAR (9), RASTAMON (4), VAN DOREN (2)

OVERVIEW:MICHEN ROY (11) is first up from a break with no trial, but looks very well suited with the concession claim, despite the draw and needing the right tempo. He can do it tough, or the expected mile rate here may even be able to overcome them with one run. His record this track and distance is positive. EAGLE MAJOR (3) finds a suitable race after racing up in class his past few runs. He was a winner here four runs back in a very similar line up where he was too strong coming off the pace. He can show reasonable gate speed, but there’s quicker ones of the gate inside and outside him so the map is crucial. TYPHOON (10) has only had the four starts but has managed two wins, on both occasions leading all the way. He must overcome the back row draw now but looks well in the mix with the concession. MUSSEL SHOALS (1) and MADAM REACTOR (4) look the most likely to fight out the early lead, and although they are both going ok that early burn may hurt. If either were to find the front and get a good time of it, their chances improve greatly. SELECTIONS:MICHEN ROY (11), EAGLE MAJOR (3), TYPHOON (10), MUSSEL SHOALS (1)

OVERVIEW:MAMMALS REASON (3) has had three runs for the new stable, and although they have been in easier grade they’ve been full of merit winning two from three. She’s been given a good trip each time, and you can expect that again from one of the tracks most prolific drivers. ELLEEGANT LANE (5) has been racing ok this season and was ok last start at Cranbourne in a race more challenging than she meets here. She should get a nice drag across with the speed and map well. ELIZA JANE (10) galloped away last start, costing itself all chance as favourite. Her two runs prior to that were quite good, and although must overcome a tricky draw this lineup isn’t overly strong. OUR MYSTERY BET (7) found the line well last week and does race well over the middle trip. Just not sure how things work out from this tricky draw. NORTHERN TERROR (7) last three have been far from ideal but now gets Herbertson and a likely soft map behind potential leader STANDANDELIVER (2) who has been racing better his past few, particularly from front row draws. SELECTIONS:MAMMALS REASON (3), ELLEEGANT LANE (5), ELIZA JANE (10), STANDANDELIVER (2)

OVERVIEW: Another very tricky race to start. MISS HERMES (6) is ready to return to her best form in this grade and looks suited with the mare’s allowance. In similar grade last week, she got a nice drive and went close in finishing 2nd. There’s plenty of speed inside of her, but if she can slide across and get a handy position. She has a good record at this track and with even luck can return to the winners list. MYNAMEISRUBY (4) returns to the front row after starting outside the back row last week. She was winner in front three back and regularly looks to lead from these draws over the mile and gets the ace driver at this track aboard. ARRAPS (3) could be open to improvement at this level and from this draw. His best form is indicated by his last win in April where from the front line was able to lead and was too strong. There’s speed inside and out but may get a nice map to put his best foot forward. TOMMYS LOOKOUT (5) has a sticky draw to contend with but has been racing well in similar company. He was a winner beating many of these off the back row last month. ATOMIC GLORY (2) ran home well last time and has claims, as does KNOW THE SCORE (8) who is racing ok but will need a plenty of luck from the draw. SELECTIONS:MISS HERMES (6), MYNAMEISRUBY (4), ARRAPS (3), TOMMYS LOOKOUT (5)

OVERVIEW: Another challenging race in a difficult Early Quaddie. MIKI MARK (8) is awkwardly drawn but well placed with Tasmyn Potter’s claim. His performances this campaign have had merit, often in stronger company. There’s a chance there could be a decent tempo the way the front-line shapes, and if the breaks come late can be in the finish. OLLY ODD POTTS (3) was very good last start, unfortunately, she’s proven a little inconsistent in backing performances up however. She drifted back last week but could map closer now and go close. FINAL BOW (7) from a better draw could have started favourite her, having beaten many of these. She will need luck but she’s always a consideration in this class. CLIVES GIRL (5) always is popular in the market in these races but has been a bit costly. This does however look to be another suitable assignment, so is worth keeping safe. The chances don’t end there with DREAMTIME NALA (4), AMADA VILLMA (6) and ALCATRAZ GIRL (9) capable of improvement with the right runs. SELECTIONS:MIKI MARK (8), OLLY ODD POTTS (3), FINAL BOW (7), CLIVES GIRL (5)

OVERVIEW: ALTO CORRAGIO (8) is giving away experience here as a 2yo having his second start, but his performance on debut here last week was solid after looking good at the trials. He looks to potentially get a good run through and map well over the short trip, and with added fitness and the inform stable, looks a winning chance. TOUCH OF REALITY (1) is nearing a win after finishing 2nd last time out as favourite at Melton, albeit having every chance. She has enough speed to kick up from the pole and have options from there tactically. PICTURE BOY (2) joins an astute stable after stepping out in a maiden at Wagga in good time. The winner of that race was average subsequently, so it’s hard to read that form, but is worth keeping safe. JUST MY LUCK (10) is first up from a break and has trialled well into this. There’s ability there, but he has a tricky draw to overcome, but don’t dismiss. BACK: ALTO CORRAGIO (8) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: ALTO CORRAGIO (8), TOUCH OF REALITY (1), PICTURE BOY (2), JUST MY LUCK (10)

OVERVIEW: JOE LOU (7) has been racing in career best form the past couple of months and finds a suitable race here despite the wide draw. He can afford an aggressive drive forward here based on how he’s been racing winning three if his past five, and although he went down as favourite last start, the winner simply had a better trip and can return to winning form. WHATS THE TEA (5) has been racing in the same races as the top pick, and going well, but now gets the advantage of a better draw to roll forward. He’s a grinding type who if on the pace will be swinging to the finish. KALARNEY PRINCE (3) returns to the front row and can be open to sharp improvement with his early gate speed, and likely to take cover and map well from the draw. LITTLE TEDEY (4) tends to run his best races from good draws and could be a knockout chance if they happen to overdo things. BACK: JOE LOU (7)– 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: JOE LOU (7), WHATS THE TEA (5), KALARNEY PRINCE (3), LITTLE TEDEY (4)

OVERVIEW:SO SKEPTICAL (5) produced a performance on debut that was hard to miss, galloping at the start, giving them a big start, only to catch the field and come late to only miss by a metre. She meets a much stronger opposition here, but to the eye when she trotted soundly, she looked pretty smart, so hoping that outing settles her to produce her best. IJUSTCANTSEEIT (4) has already proven her ability in two preparations, winning the Vicbred Homegrown as a 2yo, and even having a crack at the NSW Trotters Oaks as a 3yo. She’s trialled ok into this, and commands respect as the likely favourite and testing material. MAJESTIC YANKEE (7) won two starts ago and defeated the horse who beat the top pick last week, so the form lines are ok. Her manners let her down last time but is worth keeping safe. MINI MIA (1) was a winner from the same draw three runs back and looked to have every hope last time when fancied. She has minor claims from the soft draw. BACK: SO SKEPTICAL (5)– 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: SO SKEPTICAL (5), IJUSTCANTSEEIT (4), MAJESTIC YANKEE (7), MINI MIA (1)

OVERVIEW:STRAIGHT TO THETOP (5) seems well placed under the mobile conditions back to the short trip, as she’s a mare who possesses good early gate speed and is a good chance of crossing to the pegs first here. She was a good winner two runs back under the stand conditions and was sound again last start when well supported. She likes this track and if she does find the top will be hard to catch. JILLIBY TOPGUN (4) is enjoying his best campaign yet, winning 5 from 14. He was a little out of his grade last time and can bounce back here on his home track where he races best and back to a suitable grade. TRIPOD (3) could be a roughie open to improvement, as this is by far the easiest race he’s contested in quite a while. In saying that, he hasn’t won in three years, but he’s worth including considering the class drop and record at this track. KENNYS SON (2) turned in his most indifferent run of his preparation in SA last start, where he didn’t bring his best manners. His form prior was sound and looks set to get the right run. BACK: STRAIGHT TO THETOP (5)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:STRAIGHT TO THETOP (5), JILLIBY TOPGUN (4), TRIPOD (3), KENNYS SON (2)
